newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent up on Kuwait news, but still in range.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent up on Kuwait news, but still in range.

text.p: June Brent crude futures were firmer in Asia on Thursday, supported by Kuwait reporting an Iraqi shooting incident, but prices held within an established range, brokers said.
June Brent crude was last traded on SIMEX at $18.15 per barrel, up nine cents from London's settlement overnight of $18.06.

The rise was sparked by news that the official Kuwait News Agency reported late Wednesday that the emirate complained to the United Nations about an April 12 incident in which it said an Iraqi boat opened fire on two Kuwaiti vessels.

Brokers said the news added to another bullish element in the market after after Iraq ignored U.S. warnings not to violate the no-fly zone by flying helicopters to the Saudi border to collect Haj pilgrims.

However, brokers said they would not expect an aggressive reaction in the market until there were signs that the United Nations might take action over the incidents that could jeopardise Iraqi oil exports.
Otherwise, front-month Brent was still in the established range of $17.54 to $18.35.
